title: The Watcher's file: a GM-only record per PC of what the adversary has actually observed
summary: One record per player character holding only what the Watcher has observed through in-fiction channels (rolled Recall Knowledge, fights it watched, in-character messages, letters, phone use, journals). It is the hard gate that keeps the Claude-played adversary fair: it may only exploit what is recorded as known. The core and schema are built; filling the records from the session harvest is not.
description:
Approved by Ingram on 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #32, N10: "Yes."), after the Casebook proposed it as the first thing worth building for the Watcher, which Claude plays (LEDGER #31). It turns 'convincingly fair, not omniscient' from an aspiration into a data constraint, as the watcher-recall-knowledge-on-party idea first proposed.

Built: data/schema/watcher-file.schema.json (the shape); module/blank-inheritance/scripts/core/watcher-file.mjs (pure logic: emptyWatcherFile, recordObservation, knows, believes, canExploit, summarise); data/watcher/README.md (the rules, and where records live); test/tier1-watcher-file.test.mjs.

Rules enforced in code: in-fiction sources only, with anything flagged out of character refused (nothing real about a player is ever recorded); a plain failed Recall Knowledge teaches nothing; a critical failure is recorded as a mistaken belief the Watcher will act on but can never 'exploit'; canExploit opens only for true, recorded knowledge.

Two guards, also tested: data/watcher/ is not in the campaign-data sync allow-list (it must never reach the Foundry server, where a player's browser could fetch it), and nothing in the synced data directories may say who plays the Watcher or that it reads the players' writing (the players are not told, D14).
sourceContext: The Casebook, version 2 (B3.2, N10), and Ingram's answer in LEDGER #32.
openSubQuestions: Filling the records: which harvest feeds them first (chat-log-knowledge-base's scraped rolls, the in-universe correspondence sync, player journals, combat logs), and whether Claude writes them between sessions or the module writes them live.
How the GM sees a PC's file at the table: a panel in the Director's console, or only between sessions.
Whether a PC who deliberately feeds the Watcher false messages should be modelled as a separate 'planted' observation, so the party's counter-play is visible in the record.
